title: DCF, Multiples & Quick Valuation Math
description: Master rapid valuation estimates using DCF reasoning, comparable multiples, and investment sizing under uncertainty.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company earns $50M in free cash flow, growing 15% annually. Using a 10% discount rate and 3% terminal growth rate, which is closest to its terminal value?

options.text: ~$820M based on final-year FCF of $57.5M
~$1.45B using Year-5 FCF in Gordon Growth
~$500M since terminal value equals 10x FCF
~$2.5B by summing all future cash flows

interactions.teachingPreamble: A DCF's terminal value often accounts for 60-80% of total enterprise value. You estimate it using the Gordon Growth Model: TV = FCF₅ × (1+g) / (r−g), where g is long-term growth and r is the discount rate. For quick estimation, grow the current FCF forward 5 years, then apply the formula.

interactions.prompt: Three public SaaS companies: Firm A trades at 12x revenue (40% growth), Firm B at 8x revenue (20% growth), Firm C at 15x revenue (25% growth). You're valuing a private SaaS firm growing at 30% with $100M revenue. What's the most important signal?

options.text: Average all three multiples and apply 11.7x
Firm C is overvalued, so exclude it entirely
Growth-adjusted multiples reveal Firm A is best comp
Use Firm B since it's the most conservative

interactions.prompt: A D2C brand has $200M revenue, 20% EBITDA margins, and trades at 2x revenue. Using EV/EBITDA, what implied EBITDA multiple is the market assigning?

options.text: 5x EBITDA
10x EBITDA
15x EBITDA
20x EBITDA

interactions.teachingPreamble: Revenue multiples and EBITDA multiples are mathematically linked through margins. If a company trades at Nx revenue with M% EBITDA margins, its implied EV/EBITDA = N / M. This shortcut lets you instantly translate between multiples and sanity-check valuations without a spreadsheet.

interactions.prompt: In a DCF, increasing the discount rate from 10% to 12% while holding cash flows constant will ____ the present value, with the effect being most pronounced on cash flows occurring ____ in the future.

options.text: Decrease; further
Increase; further
Decrease; nearer
Increase; nearer

interactions.prompt: You're sizing a Series B investment in a fintech at $500M pre-money. Revenue is $30M growing 80% YoY, but unit economics turn positive only at $100M revenue. Do you invest $75M for 13% ownership, or negotiate $50M at $350M pre-money for 12.5%?

options.text: $75M at $500M—pay up for high-growth winners
$50M at $350M—protect downside before unit economics prove out
Pass entirely—negative unit economics is a dealbreaker
Offer $75M at $350M for 17.6% to maximize ownership

interactions.prompt: Shopify trades at 14x forward revenue. A private e-commerce platform has $80M ARR growing 50%. Applying a 30% illiquidity discount and 20% size discount, what's a reasonable enterprise value estimate?

options.text: ~$630M after both discounts applied to $1.12B
~$1.12B using Shopify's multiple directly
~$450M after a combined 60% discount
~$900M applying only the illiquidity discount

interactions.teachingPreamble: When using public comparables to value private companies, you must adjust for illiquidity (typically 20-35% discount) and size (10-30% discount). These discounts compound multiplicatively: if base value is $1B, a 30% illiquidity and 20% size discount gives $1B × 0.70 × 0.80 = $560M, not $1B × 0.50.

interactions.prompt: You're quickly estimating whether a $2B acquisition of a marketplace business is reasonable. Rank these sanity checks from most to least important in establishing confidence in the valuation.

options.text: Implied EV/EBITDA vs. comparable marketplace transactions
Implied price per user vs. monetization per user
Back-of-envelope DCF breakeven year check
Revenue CAGR needed to justify price at exit multiples

interactions.prompt: Interest rates just jumped from 4% to 7%, and the target's largest customer (25% of revenue) announced they're switching providers. How does this change your valuation approach?

options.text: Raise discount rate and haircut revenue—value drops 40-50%
Only adjust the discount rate; customer loss is speculative
Switch entirely to asset-based valuation as DCF is unreliable
Keep valuation unchanged but add an earnout clause

interactions.priorContext: Previously you were valuing the $2B marketplace acquisition using comparable multiples and a DCF at a 10% discount rate, with stable revenue assumptions. Now macroeconomic conditions and company fundamentals have both deteriorated simultaneously.
